task_text: Pull Lever: A wall stands in front of the hovering aerial manipulator with a lever mounted on its front face: a bar sticking straight out of the wall toward the robot from a small dark-grey base, ending in a horizontal crossbar handle. The lever pivots at the base about a horizontal axis parallel to the wall. Pull the lever up: rotate it so its free end rises by more than 40 degrees from its starting direction, perpendicular to the wall (its travel ends at 45 degrees). Success: Success when the revolute joint lever_joint has position > 40 degrees = 0.698132 rad (lever_pull_angle_min; strict inequality), i.e. the bar's free end is raised more than 40 degrees from the wall normal. The joint ranges from -pi/4 to pi/4 rad and starts at 0 rad every reset; positive is free end up, so pushing the lever down never counts. AM-Bench also reports subtask criteria lever_engaged (joint position >= 0.05 x 0.698132 = 0.034907 rad) and lever_pulled (the success condition); they are informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 20 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 2400 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 2399th step.
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where AM-Bench's success check holds, when the task's episode length of 20 s of simulated time runs out (AM-Bench's time-out, at control step 2399), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
